summary: Kodo Nomura (1882–1963) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Koho Sawada, Sotan Oka, and Join Saeki, and held posts as professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Kodo Yamada (1866–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University studying under Shiro Matsumoto, and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg.

Koen Wellens specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under the doctoral supervision of Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at KU Leuven (~1980–1999), where he earned an MA, and at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1993).

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a doctorate from the University of Tokyo in 1928. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1959–1962) and held multiple roles at Komazawa University, including president in 1976.
Koichi Hiraoka specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1984) and held a post as visiting professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Koichi Hokazono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn and Kyushu University, where he earned a PhD and held a post attested in 1995, later serving as professor at Kagoshima International University.

Koichi Shinohara works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and as senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, subsequently serving there as assistant (2005), project researcher (2015), and professor (attested 2026).

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an MA at the University of Tokyo, studying under Akira Hirakawa and Gyōin Hashimoto, and served as associate professor at Rikkyo University (~1974–2006).
Koin Takada (1924–1998) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1944) and under Gyōin Hashimoto, whom he succeeded in 1967.

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara, later lecturing at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and serving as a staff member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Shindo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies and served as a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University, where he served as associate professor (~1968–1999) and professor (~1977–1999).

Koji Tanaka works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Macquarie University, the University of Auckland's Department of Philosophy (attested 2011–2014), and the Australian National University's School of Philosophy.

Kojiro Yoshikawa (1904–1980) was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as professor of Chinese language and literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and president of Toho Gakkai (~1972–1980).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate from Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda and served as professor there (1941–1969), while also serving as president of Taisho University.
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and held an appointment as lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
